payload.recallText: This is the last unit of my class today. I teach third grade and we are on the last unit. We are studying the Oregon Trail. I like to use games to teach my classes. The kids come up with funny names. I don't know how I am going to teach the Oregon Trail, which is really serious stuff, as a game. So I decide to treat the journey like a game. We have covered wagons and each person gets their own name. One day I get to class and this smart Alec kid, Alex, asks , me if anyone is going to die. I forgot that people actually died on the Oregon Trail. So the next day I get to class and put my bonnet on and say today someone might die. So we are on the trail and the wagon hits a rock and tips over. It traps a girl underneath, Katie.  She is caught with the wagon on her legs. We roll again and she hasn't died, and we are able to get the wagon off of her. But her legs are infected. She asks if she is going to die. I imagine that I am getting a call from parents asking why their kid died in class. I am starting to regret having someone die on the trail. Then a girl in the class speaks up and says she is a doctor. So she offers to help the girl with the infected legs. She has to roll the dice to see if the girl dies from the infection or if they can save her. If she rolls a six, the girl dies. Otherwise, she lives. The doctor doesn't roll a six so the girl lives, and I am so glad no one died. I learned that the kids love the danger though and I am the only one that doesn't. The next day we talk about wild animals on the trail. They ask if one of the animals is going to die. I say no, it is injured and we are going to take care of it. We adopt a wolf and it follow us to Oregon City. We get to Oregon City in record time. I ran into the girl who almost died on the Oregon trail later in life, when she was in the 9th grade. She looked the same only stretched out, and she asked if I remember the time she almost died.
